_meta.title: Motorsport world championships outside Formula 1
_meta.purpose: Feeds the Zone Zero Cup motorsport recognition bonus. Formula 1 is not listed here; it is read live from public/data/f1/data.json.
_meta.test: Any top-tier championship with a season-long drivers' title is credited. How international the field is sets the weight, not whether the series is admitted. An earlier draft excluded a series whose champions were all one nationality, which put NASCAR among the national sports; Ashwin overruled it on 2026-09-04 and NASCAR is here with a weight that reflects a domestic field.

excluded.World Endurance Championship / Le Mans: Titles are won by two- and three-driver crews of mixed nationality. Attribution to one nation is not merely uncertain, it is ambiguous by construction.
excluded.Isle of Man TT / Dakar: Event wins, not a championship. No season-long title to decay.
excluded.Junior single-seaters (F2, F3, Moto2, Mo: Feeder series. Crediting them would count the same driver twice on the way up.

_meta.weights: Weight reflects how deep and how international the field is, and whether the series holds world championship status. Formula 1 is the 1.00 anchor.
_meta.window: 1990 onward. With an 8-year half-life a 1990 title is already worth 0.04 of a current one, so earlier seasons cannot move a ranking.
_meta.podiums: Added 2026-09-04. Every other title pillar on this board counts champion, runner-up and third; motorsport counted winners only, which understated it twice over. It lost the second and third of every season, and it lost every nation that has been on a championship podium without ever winning one. Scored 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25, the same ratio as the world tier in TIER (4.0 / 2.0 / 1.0).
_meta.gaps: Speedway 1990 second place is omitted. Shawn Moran finished second on points and was disqualified for a failed drug test, and sources disagree on whether the FIM vacated the position or retained him as a disqualified second. An omitted position is honest; a guessed one is not.

series.label: Formula 1
series.why: The apex of the sport and the 1.00 anchor for every other weight. Champions are read live from the site's own F1 pipeline, so only the rest of the podium is kept here. The 1997 order is the final one after Schumacher's exclusion.

series.label: MotoGP
series.why: Two-wheel racing's apex, an FIM world championship on a global calendar. A smaller commercial footprint than Formula 1 and a shorter grid.

series.label: World Rally Championship
series.why: An FIA world championship with a genuinely global calendar, but usually only two or three factory teams contest the title.

series.label: IndyCar
series.why: Single-country venues but a champion list spanning five continents, and the Indianapolis 500 carries prestige no other oval race has. The 1996 to 2007 CART and IRL titles are each credited at half, because the sport was split and neither crown was the whole field.

series.label: Speedway
series.why: A genuine world championship with real national depth in Poland and Scandinavia, and the only motorsport with a working national-team competition. The competitive world is small, so the weight is low. Seasons are recorded by the year the title was decided.

series.label: Formula E
series.why: World championship status only since 2021, and its grid draws on the same driver pool one tier down from Formula 1. Seasons are recorded by the year they finished.

series.label: NASCAR Cup Series
series.why: The largest stock car championship in the world and the second most watched motorsport on television, but a domestic field: every Cup champion since 1990 has been American. The weight matches IndyCar's, which races the same country with a field drawn from five continents. Champions are recorded by year and nationality only, because the nationality has been American in every season in the window and no attribution question turns on which American won.
